newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen premier says inflations drops to 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Yemen premier says inflations drops to 10 pct.

text.p: Economic reforms have enabled Yemen to drive annual inflation down to 10 percent last year from 120 percent in 1994, the impoverished Arab state's prime minister said on Wednesday.
"The inflation rate has fallen from 120 percent in 1994 to 10 percent by the end of 1996 due to the economic reform programme," Abdul-Aziz Abdul-Ghani told a news conference.
Yemen launched an economic reform programme in March 1995 in agreement with the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank.
Abdel-Ghani said unemployment was still high but added accurate statistics on the jobless rate were not available.
Economists in Sanaa estimate unemployment ranges between 35 to 50 percent.
